title: Vyshka telemetry envelope bodies
description: Machine-readable companion to spec/protocol.md section 8.1. The prose document is normative: where the two disagree, the prose wins. Like the other schema documents this is a library of definitions with no root constraint: reference `#/$defs/eventBatch` for the plugin -> hub body and `#/$defs/eventReject` for the hub -> plugin refusal.

eventType.description: A {namespace}.{name} type: two or more non-empty segments of letters, digits, _ and -, separated by dots. Core types are the `core.*` list of section 8.1; everything else is a custom event and is stored, routed, and retained identically.

ts.description: When the event happened on the game server. Optional. This is what a plugin MUST send, but it is not what a hub may insist on receiving: a hub substitutes its own receipt time when ts is absent, unparseable, of the wrong JSON type, or implausibly far in the future, and never refuses an event over it alone. A hub that enforced this constraint would lose a batch of real events to one bad clock.

data.description: Type-specific payload, bounded by the hub (reference cap 16 KiB, measured on the raw bytes of the serialized value). Absent and null both read as an empty object.

eventBatch.title: event.batch body
eventBatch.description: Plugin -> hub. A batch is accepted or refused whole: a hub that refuses one stores none of its events, because the ack is per envelope and there is no per-event receipt a plugin could reconcile a partial accept against.

events.description: Up to 200 events. An empty array is a plugin flushing nothing: legal, and it stores nothing.

eventReject.title: event.reject body
eventReject.description: Hub -> plugin, queued when a batch was refused. Envelope-level success: the refused envelope is still acked, the session stays up, and the plugin must not treat this as a transport error. The events it names are gone, and this notice is the visible counter section 9.4 requires.

envelopeId.description: The id of the event.batch envelope this rejection answers.

path.description: A path into the rejected body, such as events[3].t. Empty when the fault is the body as a whole.

errors.description: Bounded by the hub (reference cap 20 entries); a batch wrong in more ways than that is wrong enough to fix iteratively.
